page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 2500 GB local NVMe SSD and a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps. Acceleration hardware is not included, with GPU count standing at zero.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier memory subsystem throughput, reflected by a PassMark memory score of 2999.09, which ranks in the top 10%. Memory read bandwidth reaches 462.24 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks and 108.09 GB/sec for 256 MB blocks. Synthetic CPU tests show average performance across Geekbench single-core (1863.0) and multi-core (5941.0) suites, as well as stress-ng multi-core (6814.57). Decompression throughput is strong, with single-threaded bzip3 reaching 14.44 GB/sec. Conversely, PassMark CPU tests show weaker results, particularly in encryption tests at 752.76, and LLM text generation is restricted by the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators or discrete GPUs.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance yields strong qualitative value for IOPS-intensive and memory-heavy workloads due to its large direct-attached NVMe storage and high memory-to-core allocation. The trade-off lies in standard single-thread compute capabilities and the absence of x86 vector extensions such as AVX-512. The configuration is primarily tailored for local database systems, caching tiers like Redis, log aggregation pipelines, and high-throughput transactional storage workloads requiring fast NVMe scratch disks.
description: Amazon Web Services i8ge.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, 32.0 GB of memory, and a 2500 GB local NVMe SSD, alongside a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance delivers exceptional memory performance, placing in the top 10% on PassMark memory benchmarks, with strong single-threaded decompression rates. General compute across stress-ng and Geekbench demonstrates average results, while lack of specialized vector instructions limits encryption and LLM throughput. With 8 GB of memory per core and high-capacity bundled NVMe storage, this instance is suitable for transactional databases, in-memory caching solutions like Redis, and write-heavy log processing pipelines.
